what: The counts the scribes published for a book, and nothing else. A target here is a number this project holds a source for. A number remembered, looked up, or carried in from outside the corpus is not a target and may not be written here, however confident anyone is that it is right.
the_law: A book is served when our count equals theirs on every measure they published for it. Not close. Equal. Where they published nothing we can hold, the book is not proved and is not served.
why_it_is_the_only_check_of_its_kind: Every other guard in this suite is one lane checking itself. This one is checked against arithmetic somebody else did, by hand, before any of this existed, and wrote down. The masorah finalis is the only mark in the corpus that makes a claim a machine can test, which is why recording it is not attesting it. The half must be counted.
why_it_cannot_be_passed_by_accident: Twelve rules decide what counts as a word of a book, and twenty-four books each exercise them in a different mixture. A wrong rule does not produce a constant error; it produces an error proportional to how often that rule fires in that book. Twenty-four books against twelve rules is more equations than unknowns, and there is nowhere for a wrong rule to hide: it would have to produce exactly the compensating miss in every book independently. One book is a checksum. The set is a proof.

admissibility.a_target_needs_a_source_we_hold: The source is named by its address in this corpus, and the claim must be legible there. A figure from memory or from a reference work we do not hold is not admissible, whatever it says.
admissibility.measures: verses, words, letters. Whichever a book's own note publishes. A book may carry one, two, or all three.
admissibility.the_verdict_is_all_or_nothing: A book passes when it holds at least one target and every target it holds matches exactly. One target missing its number withholds the book, and the others matching does not soften that.

known_and_not_admitted.why_not: carried in from outside the corpus. It was used on 2026-09-04 to establish that a maqaf separates two words rather than joining one, and it did that job, but it is not a source this project holds and it may not gate a book until it is.
same. Widely published as the figure for a scroll; we hold no copy of the claim, and the count it is compared against came out one letter short with no cause found.

known_and_not_admitted.claim: per-book verse totals for the five books of the Torah
known_and_not_admitted.why_not: same, and one of them was wrong. Exodus was carried in as 1,209 and the note this project actually holds says 1,210, which is what our own count produces. The remembered figure was the error, not the text.

source.says_in_english: one thousand two hundred and ten verses, as may be shown from the masorah itself, which wrote at 'you shall not revile' that this is the half of the book in verses
source.carries_its_own_proof: the note does not only give a total, it names the verse where the half falls. Our count puts that verse at 606 of 1,210, the second of the two middle verses, which is where the note puts it.

targets.note: No zone for this book exists. The target stands and gates nothing until one does.

what_is_not_here.says: Twenty-three of the twenty-four books hold no target in this record. That is not a claim that the scribes published nothing for them: it is a statement that this project has not yet found what it holds. The scan on 2026-09-04 looked in two places and found nothing usable — the served shelf, which carries no biblical book at all, and the corpus lane's restored Miqra, whose books end on their last verse and carry no finalis rows. The corpus body for the thirty-nine biblical files has not been searched.
